decisions.reason: As a core process-equipment launch tied to the firm's innovation path, it carries enough sunk engineering, documentation and channel investment that management would likely continue backing it and explain any weaker uptake as temporary or niche-specific.

This resin injection unit is also close to the firm's core application technology, so public commitment, prior investment and the tendency to justify earlier launch decisions make withdrawal within the next year unlikely.

A manual airless spray gun fits the company's established range especially well, and a German machinery firm with service obligations and a global distributor base would usually retain such a product unless there were clear persistent failure.

Because E is a broader line with several models, the firm has made the most visible and extensive commitment here, so escalation of commitment and portfolio logic both strongly favor keeping it on the market.
